title: Zelenskyy says Ukraine got no warning before Russian strike
excerpt: Officials in Kyiv said a 21-year-old woman was killed in the attack, and Zelenskyy said the barrage left more than half a million people without power, heat or running water.
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Monday that Russia launched overnight strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure without advance warning from partner countries before the first wave of the attack.

“Once again, Russia launched a ballistic missile attack in multiple waves throughout the night, and once again, there was no warning from our partners,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media, according to The Guardian. Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said on television that Ukraine had not received a warning before the first wave, which hit power plants in Kyiv at around 11 p.m. Sunday.

The reporting differed on the second wave of strikes. The Guardian said Ihnat told television viewers that Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike at 3 a.m. Later reports from the New York Post and the Los Angeles Times said information about the second wave arrived too late for air raid sirens to be activated in time.

Zelenskyy later said the barrage hit 28 substations and other critical energy facilities, leaving more than a half-million people without electricity, heat and running water. Earlier NBC News reporting, published before those later versions, said the attack damaged more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities across Ukraine. The later figure supersedes the earlier count in the updated reporting.

Officials in Kyiv said a 21-year-old woman was killed in the capital. Zelenskyy also said Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region.

The Russian Defense Ministry said it struck targets including a data center, a logistics hub storing components for drones and cruise missiles, an industrial facility making drone components and a locomotive depot where missiles are stored, according to the same reports. That claim was the ministry’s account of the strike.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Monday he had no information about the previous night’s attack. The Guardian quoted Rubio as saying, “If it happened last night, I don’t know exactly. I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system.”

Zelenskyy said in the same social media post that Ukraine “never wanted this war” and had welcomed “literally EVERY attempt” by partners to bring it to a dignified end. He added that the war continues because of Russian strikes and Moscow’s desire to drag it out.

source_conflicts: Source 1 says Yurii/Yuri Ihnat said Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike at about 3 a.m.; Sources 2 and 4, later versions of the same general reporting, say information about the second wave arrived too late for air raid sirens to be activated in time. The article properly notes this difference.

https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/o: Zelenskyy said there was no warning from partners before the first wave of the overnight multi-wave attack.
Ihnat said on television that Ukraine had not received a warning before the first wave, which hit Kyiv power plants at about 11 p.m.
The Guardian version said Ukraine did receive a warning before a successive strike at 3 a.m.
Rubio said: "If it happened last night, I don’t know exactly. I know a few nights ago there was a software problem involving their early warning system."
https://nypost.com/2026/10/19/world-news: Later reporting said information about the second wave arrived too late for air raid sirens to be activated in time.
Zelenskyy said the barrage hit 28 substations and other critical energy facilities and deprived more than a half-million people of electricity, heat and running water.
Zelenskyy said Russia fired 16 ballistic missiles at Kyiv and the surrounding region.
Officials in Kyiv reported that a 21-year-old woman was killed.
The Russian Defense Ministry said it struck a data center, a logistics hub, an industrial facility and a locomotive depot.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine "never wanted this war" and had welcomed "literally EVERY attempt" by partners to end it.
https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/ze: Earlier NBC News reporting said the barrage damaged more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities across Ukraine.
NBC also reported more than a half-million people were deprived of light/heating/running water and that 16 ballistic missiles were fired at Kyiv and nearby areas.
https://www.latimes.com/world-nation/sto: Later reporting matched Source 2 on the 28 facilities figure, the more than half-million affected, the 16 ballistic missiles, the 21-year-old woman killed, and the second-wave warning arriving too late for sirens.

fc.summary: No factual errors found against the supplied sources. The article accurately centers the latest development, attributes official and Russian claims, and correctly describes the differing source accounts about warning before the second wave.

log.summary: Recast the article to lead with Zelenskyy’s warning complaint, added the first-wave and second-wave warning accounts in chronological order, and clarified that the Russian Defense Ministry strike description was its own claim. I also restored the later, more specific damage figure while preserving the earlier report as an earlier version of the coverage.
